Title: July 30, 2026 - City of Boulder City Council Special Meeting (Tip Offset Ordinance 8754 Second Reading and Public Hearing; Wildfire Resilience on Open Space Ballot Measure Direction)

Topic1.Title: Roll Call, Quorum, and Agenda Amendment
Topic1.Summary: The Mayor called the special meeting to order and the council took roll call, confirming a quorum. The council voted unanimously to amend the agenda to add item 4A, direction on wildfire resilience on open space ballot measure.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda Approval
Topic2.Summary: Council considered consent agenda item 2, consisting of items 2A and 2B, and approved them unanimously by roll call vote.

Topic3.Title: Second Reading and Public Hearing on Tip Offset Ordinance 8754
Topic3.Summary: Staff presented proposed Ordinance 8754 amending the minimum wage chapter to set a local tip offset amount for food and beverage workers, outlining four options and community survey results. Restaurant industry data showed slowing sales, jobs, and visits, while most surveyed workers favored no change to the offset.

Topic4.Title: Council Questions on Tip Offset Presentation
Topic4.Summary: Council members asked about whether the sales tax chart was inflation adjusted and questioned how the status quo option was presented as restaurant savings of $62,800, which staff explained as the amount restaurants currently save under the existing $3.32 offset.

Topic5.Title: Public Hearing on Tip Offset Ordinance
Topic5.Summary: Roughly 28 residents, labor organizers, restaurant workers, business representatives, students, and online participants spoke at two-minute limits. Most urged keeping the scheduled minimum wage increases and the current tip offset, citing rising rents and cost of living, while the Boulder Chamber, Colorado Restaurant Association, and Downtown Boulder Partnership asked for a collaborative task force and relief for restaurants.

Topic6.Title: Council Discussion and Decision on Tip Offset
Topic6.Summary: Council members expressed sympathy for both workers and restaurant owners and broad support for a task force including labor, business, landlords, and experts. Several members said they would keep the current minimum wage schedule, and no motion was made to amend the ordinance, so the existing schedule will proceed.

Topic7.Title: Direction on Wildfire Resilience on Open Space Ballot Measure
Topic7.Summary: Staff sought council direction on whether to pursue a charter amendment or code change for wildfire resilience on open space, noting the Open Space Board of Trustees recommended a charter amendment while staff recommended a code change. Council agreed not to pursue a ballot measure this year and to consider an ordinance instead, with an executive session for legal advice before further action.
